tools.name: studio_info
tools.description: What Squatch Stack (a software and hardware studio in the Missouri Ozarks) builds, and how to reach it.

tools.name: list_goods
tools.description: Browse the Squatch Stack shop (tees, mugs, hats, stickers, posters, totes). Optional text search and kind filter. Prices in USD; tax and shipping are added at checkout.

tools.name: show_shop
tools.description: Show the Squatch Stack goods as an interactive shop the person can browse: photos, colours and sizes, and a Buy button that opens the shop's secure checkout in their browser. Use it when someone wants to look around or buy. Optional search words or kind narrow it. Apps without interactive views get

tools.name: get_good
tools.description: Details for one Squatch Stack product by slug: description, every variant (color/size) with its variant_id and price.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Build a Squatch Stack checkout link for the chosen variants. It does NOT buy anything: give the link to the person, who reviews the cart and pays on the shop's secure checkout (tax and shipping calculated there).

tools.name: search_walks
tools.description: Find essays from 'Wild Man of the Way' (24 walks on theplainlystated.com) by words, thinker (e.g. Zhuangzi, Seneca, Thoreau) or format. Returns titles, short excerpts and links.

tools.name: get_walk
tools.description: One 'Wild Man of the Way' essay by number (1-24): title, thinkers, reading time, an opening excerpt and the link to read it in full.

tools.name: contact_draft
tools.description: Make a ready-to-send email link (mailto) to Squatch Stack with a fitting subject and body. It sends nothing; the person opens it in their mail app.

tools.name: parse_buffalo
tools.description: Tag every word of a 'Buffalo buffalo ...' sentence as city, animal or verb, with a plain-English gloss.

tools.name: pick_a_walk
tools.description: Suggest one 'Wild Man of the Way' essay that fits the minutes someone has right now, with a short excerpt and the link. Different each time.

tools.name: request_custom
tools.description: Leave a request in the Squatch Stack inbox: a custom shirt or piece, details or an update on something, help with an order, or anything else. A person reads every one and answers from hello@squatch.cc if an email address is given. Returns a reference (SQ-XXXXXX) to check with request_status. It send

tools.name: request_status
tools.description: Where a request sent with request_custom has got to (received, read, replied, closed), and the studio's answer. With the private token (SQ-XXXXXX-XXXXXXXXXX) it shows the answer; with the short reference (SQ-XXXXXX) only the status. Never shows the original message or email address.

tools.name: about_this_server
tools.description: Who runs this server, how to verify it, exactly what each tool can and cannot do, what is kept, and the limits. Use it when someone asks whether they can trust a link or a request.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_custom, request_status · Private data: contact_draft, request_status · Public sink: contact_draft, request_custom, request_status · Destructive: search_walks.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_custom, request_status · Private data: contact_draft, request_status · Public sink: contact_draft, request_custom, request_status · Destructive: search_walks

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
